title: GitOps-driven Terraform Operator CI: policy safeguards & upgrade healthchecks
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Goal: Replace ad-hoc pipeline applies with a GitOps-driven Terraform Operator workflow that preserves strong CI policy enforcement (OPA/Conftest) and adds automated preflight and post-apply health checks for VPC/private deployments. This ticket covers the CI side: building lint/plan pipelines, policy evaluation, plan scoring & gating, and integration points with the operator reconciliation model for safe upgrades and rollouts.

Background: Private (VPC) deployments require stricter change controls and predictable upgrades. We currently allow CI apply jobs that talk directly to state backends; this causes intermittent race conditions, and lacks a unified policy evaluation step across repos. Moving to a GitOps model (PR -> plan + policy checks -> merge -> operator reconcile apply) reduces blast radius, but requires robust CI gates and automated health checks to detect regressions from provider or module upgrades.

Scope / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement CI pipeline steps for all private-deploy Terraform repos: fmt, validate, tflint, tfsec, terraform plan (in PR) with OPA/Conftest policy evaluation against the plan JSON.
- Produce a deterministic "policy score" artifact for each plan; fail the pipeline for score < threshold and create comments on PR with remediation hints.
- Wire pipeline to a mandatory plan-approve check: manual approval allowed only for P1/P0 with documented justification; otherwise merges blocked until score passes.
- Integrate pipeline with the Terraform Operator by writing the approved PR to the GitOps repo used by the operator; the operator will handle apply reconciliation. CI must annotate the commit with the policy artifact checksum and link to plan output.
- Implement canary workspace tagging: allow staged apply to a small subset of resources (network peering, minimal subnets) before full reconcile for high-risk changes.
- Add automated preflight healthcheck job that runs after operator reconcile (post-apply): check VPC route tables, stub endpoint reachability, DNS resolution for private endpoints, and smoke test connectivity from bastion to internal services. Failures create incidents and trigger automatic rollback runbook.
- Add a nightly drift detection job that runs terraform plan against active workspaces and surfaces unexpected diffs to the teams dashboard.
- Document runbooks, alerting channels (Slack + PagerDuty), and rollback procedures for state restore/previous successful commit reapply.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Operator vs pipeline apply: we chose GitOps + Operator to centralize state mutation and reduce concurrent apply conflicts. Trade-off: introduces dependence on operator health and adds latency between merge and apply; mitigated by canary workspaces and realtime healthchecks.
- Policy enforcement location: evaluate as early as possible (PR plan) to give fast feedback to authors. Keep secondary runtime enforcement via admission checks in the operator for safety.
- Policy tooling: standardize on Rego for cluster-level rules and Conftest for plan-level quick checks. OPA Rego modules will be shared across repos; Conftest wrappers will produce the human-friendly scorecard.
- Rollback strategy: prefer reapplying the last-known-good git commit to the operator GitOps repo rather than attempting automated tfstate surgery. This keeps restores auditable but requires good state snapshots.

Implementation approach:
1) Create a reusable GitHub Actions workflow (or CircleCI job) template: terraform-fmt/validate -> tflint -> tfsec -> terraform-plan (json) -> conftest eval -> opa scoring -> upload artifacts (plan.json, score.json).
2) Add a small Lambda/GitHub app that posts formatted plan+score comments on PRs and creates a merge-blocking status check.
3) Extend the operator GitOps repo conventions to accept a metadata file next to manifests: {"policy_checksum": "sha256...", "plan_artifact": "url"}. CI writes this file on merge.
4) Implement post-apply healthcheck runner as a Kubernetes Job invoked by the operator after a successful apply. Healthcheck results emitted to Grafana + Slack.
5) Nightly drift job: run plan, record diffs to a Drift dashboard, and create issues for changes exceeding thresholds.

Acceptance tests:
- Create test repo with a small VPC module. Open PR with an intentional policy violation (eg. public subnet with 0.0.0.0/0 route). CI must fail with clear Remediation steps and create a comment.
- Merge a low-risk change: operator should reconcile within expected window, post-apply healthcheck must pass and dashboard reflect green.
- Simulate provider upgrade change that causes drift: nightly drift job must detect and create ENG ticket.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement operator-side admission webhooks for runtime policy enforcement (follow-up ticket planned).
- Does not cover RBAC onboarding for customers; that is handled by Private deployment team separately.

References:

- Example Conftest policies: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policies/tree/main/conftest
